request.prompt:
VIEW 2 — THE SAME MAP SEEN FROM STRAIGHT ABOVE: A TOP-DOWN PLAN, NORTH AT THE TOP OF THE FRAME. The same place, the same hand and the same moonlit night as the first image.

ONE single full-frame view. Not a grid, not panels, not insets. No text, no labels, no compass, no interface.

The frame is tall. From top to bottom:
- Top sixth: the town on its cliff terraces, about 160 blocks wide: the coach road along the very top edge, a winding high street of slate roofs stepping down, a small chapel, and at the bottom of the town a stone harbour whose basin is empty black mud with tilted boats on it. A stone breakwater leaves the harbour's east side, runs south-east into the bay, and ends in a round lighthouse.
- The middle half: a long plain of wet black mud, about 320 blocks long and much wider than the town, with black sea water showing in channels. Down its middle runs one straight line of marker stakes with small lamps, from a stone stair at the harbour to the far end. Partway down, a cluster of wrecked hulls lies beside the stake line, then a grounded salvage launch with a mast, then a pair of rows of standing carved stone pillars, then a place where the dry ground narrows to a thin ridge with water on both sides and a round dark pit in the mud beside it.
- Below the mud: a straight band of open black sea water about sixty blocks wide crosses the whole frame from side to side. At the end of the stake line a small square stone landing stage juts into it with a small slate-roofed stone ferry house on it. On the far shore, opposite, an identical small ferry house.
- Bottom third: a low bank of mud, and lying on it the creature, seen from directly above as a long vertical shape: its HEAD AT THE TOP pointing up the frame toward the town, its TAIL AT THE BOTTOM edge of the frame, its long body running straight up and down the frame, never across it. A whale-like leviathan (not a shark: no dorsal fin) built of dark grey-green and black blocks, about 140 blocks long and 60 wide, seen from its back, a ridge of spine down its back, a round blowhole behind the head, three dark torn wounds along its west flank, its tail to the south. A narrow mud ridge runs along its west side a short way off.
- Dark open ocean all round the edges.
request.style_note: The Stranding: every image in this series is one place drawn in the same hand — a Minecraft Java Edition build shown as a high-quality in-game screenshot with a soft night shader. Every surface is made of visible one-metre cubic blocks with vanilla Minecraft textures (cobblestone, stone bricks, spruce and dark oak planks and logs, deepslate, mud and packed mud, black and grey concrete, prismarine, lanterns, glass panes), crisp block edges, no smooth curves anywhere: round or organic forms are stepped block shapes. The place is a grey slate-roofed fishing town on cliff terraces above a bay, a plain of wet black mud risen from the bay, and a vast stranded sea creature built of dark blocks lying at the far edge of the mud. Night under a clear sky and a bright full moon: cold blue-silver moonlight on wet mud and slate roofs, deep blue-black shadows, small warm yellow pools of lantern light at doors and windows, sea water near-black with silver moon glints. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset, never a caption, no text, no labels, no border, no interface.
